notes: PSA 9.5 ng/mL. PI-RADS 3. PSAD 0.19. Prostate volume 49 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.64.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer diagnosis following recent biopsy upgrade to ISUP grade group 2.

The patient is a 64-year-old retired civil servant who is widowed but currently lives with a partner. He is a current smoker with a 35 pack-year history and consumes approximately 3 units of alcohol weekly. He maintains a daily walking routine of 45 minutes. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 6. His medical history includes a circumcision and recent appointments for baseline memory screening and physiotherapy for lower back pain. He has no known allergies except to iodinated contrast, which caused mild reactions. His daughter manages his communication and is copied on correspondence with his consent. He has been under urological surveillance since a prior benign biopsy, with PSA levels fluctuating between 0.8 and 9.5 ng/mL over the past three years.

On DRE, a nodule is palpable, consistent with clinical stage cT2. General examination reveals a well-nourished man with stable vital signs. There are no signs of metastatic disease or lymphadenopathy.
